name: Glasgow
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Glasgow: insurance and financial services diligence, Scottish litigation support and asset research.
hero_lede: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city, with a financial and insurance quarter, shipbuilding on the Clyde and a large public and professional services base. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, working within Scots law and alongside Scottish solicitors.
intro: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city, with about 650,300 residents in 2024 and a wider metropolitan population estimated at around 1.8 million, more than a quarter of Scotland's total. Its economy produced about £31.8 billion of output in 2023, second in Scotland only to Edinburgh. Health and social work, administrative services, retail, professional services and education are the largest employers. The International Financial Services District is one of the UK's larger financial quarters, and most of the UK's biggest general insurers have a base or head office in the city. Shipbuilding continues on the Clyde, and biosciences, software, creative industries and three universities broaden the base.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Glasgow because insurance, banking operations, shared service centres, defence manufacturing and public contracts concentrate there. Insurers need to test suspicious claims and the networks behind them; acquirers and lenders need to understand Scottish companies and their controllers; counsel need facts for actions in the sheriff court or the Court of Session. Scotland has its own legal system, courts, land registers and enforcement procedures, distinct from England and Wales, so research and any evidence gathered must be planned around Scots law and Scottish procedure rather than assumptions carried over from London.

matters.title: Insurance claims and fraud networks
matters.text: With many large general insurers operating from Glasgow, organised motor, liability and property claims fraud is a recurring concern. We research claimants, repairers, credit hire and claims management businesses, and the connections between them, using public records and open sources, to support insurers' counter-fraud teams and their solicitors.

matters.title: Scottish company and counterparty diligence
matters.text: Scottish companies are registered at Companies House but sit within Scots property, insolvency and court systems. We review filings, persons with significant control, charges, Scottish court and insolvency notices and reputational sources to identify controllers, related parties and undisclosed history before transactions or contracts.

matters.title: Asset research for diligence
matters.text: Creditors enforcing decrees in Scotland use diligence such as arrestment and inhibition rather than English enforcement tools. We map land and buildings, business interests and connected entities from Registers of Scotland and other public sources so Scottish solicitors can target diligence effectively.

matters.title: Defence and public contract suppliers
matters.text: Shipbuilding on the Clyde and a large public sector create supply chains for defence, health and local government work. We examine the ownership, litigation history and integrity record of subcontractors and bidders, supporting procurement, compliance and investigations into conflicts of interest or overbilling.

matters.title: Shared service centre misconduct
matters.text: Banks, insurers and multinationals run operations and shared service centres in Glasgow. Where internal fraud, data misuse or employee misconduct is suspected, we support investigations scoped with employment counsel, focusing on documentary analysis, open-source research and interview preparation within UK data protection rules.

local_context.title: Glasgow Sheriff Court
local_context.text: Most civil litigation in Scotland begins in the sheriff courts, and Glasgow Sheriff Court is among the busiest. Claims up to £5,000 follow simple procedure, and higher-value claims proceed as ordinary causes. Glasgow is one of the sheriff courts that offers a dedicated commercial procedure, with active case management and a specialist sheriff assigned to the dispute. Because the Court of Session now generally hears only claims of £100,000 or more, many business disputes involving Glasgow parties are heard locally.

local_context.title: Court of Session in Edinburgh
local_context.text: Scotland's supreme civil court sits in Edinburgh, not Glasgow. Its Commercial Court has specialist commercial judges and hears larger business disputes for Scottish and overseas parties, with an emphasis on swift timetables and case management. Glasgow matters of significant value are often litigated there, with appeals ultimately to the UK Supreme Court. Research for such cases is planned around Court of Session procedure and Scottish rules of evidence.

local_context.title: Diligence and sheriff officers
local_context.text: Scotland enforces decrees through diligence carried out by sheriff officers rather than through English enforcement agents. Arrestment freezes funds held by third parties such as banks or employers, and inhibition prevents a debtor from selling or burdening heritable property. A charge for payment usually precedes many steps. Asset research for Glasgow debtors is therefore framed around what Scottish diligence can reach, and enforcement itself is a matter for Scottish solicitors and sheriff officers.

local_context.title: Scottish land and property records
local_context.text: Land and buildings in Scotland are recorded by Registers of Scotland, not HM Land Registry. Title to property in Glasgow is held on the Land Register of Scotland, with some older titles still in the historic Register of Sasines. Title sheets show proprietors, securities and burdens and are a core source for asset research, though ownership through companies, trusts or overseas entities may require further work.

local_context.title: Scottish prosecution and recovery
local_context.text: Criminal investigation in Glasgow is carried out by Police Scotland, and prosecution is the responsibility of the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service rather than the Crown Prosecution Service. Civil recovery of the proceeds of crime in Scotland is pursued by a separate Scottish unit. Where a private matter may become a criminal referral, counsel decide the route, and our work is documented so that it can be handed over cleanly.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Glasgow and works on Glasgow matters from Nashville. We start with the client's Scottish solicitors, because the purpose of the work, whether a sheriff court or Court of Session action, an insurance claims review, diligence planning or a transaction, determines what research is proportionate. Sources include Companies House filings, Registers of Scotland title information, Scottish court and insolvency notices and open sources. Where local enquiries or interviews are needed, we coordinate suitably qualified local professionals and plan the work around UK data protection law and Scottish evidential rules. Reports state sources and confidence levels so solicitors and advocates can rely on them in Scottish proceedings.

faqs.q: Is a Glasgow business dispute heard in Glasgow or Edinburgh?
faqs.a: It depends mainly on value and complexity. Claims below £100,000 generally go to the sheriff court, and Glasgow Sheriff Court offers a commercial procedure for business disputes. Larger or more complex claims are often raised in the Court of Session in Edinburgh, which has its own Commercial Court. Your Scottish solicitors choose the forum, and we tailor research to it.

faqs.q: How are judgments enforced against a Glasgow debtor?
faqs.a: Scotland uses diligence, executed by sheriff officers, rather than English enforcement mechanisms. Arrestment can freeze bank balances or wages held by third parties, and inhibition can stop a debtor dealing with land or buildings. We help identify accounts, property and business interests from lawful sources so solicitors can decide which forms of diligence are worth pursuing.

faqs.q: Where are Glasgow property ownership records held?
faqs.a: Registers of Scotland maintains the Land Register of Scotland and the older Register of Sasines. Title sheets show the registered proprietor, standard securities and burdens. Where property is held through companies, partnerships or overseas entities, we combine title information with Companies House records and other filings to work out who is likely to control it.

faqs.q: Can TDSC help with insurance fraud linked to Glasgow?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. We research claimants, businesses and networks using public records, court material and open sources, and identify links between repeat parties. We do not obtain personal data unlawfully or access restricted databases. Findings are reported with sources so the insurer and its solicitors can decide whether to defend, refer to the police or pursue recovery.

faqs.q: Does Scots law change how an investigation is run?
faqs.a: Often. Scotland has its own courts, procedure, property law, enforcement system and prosecution service, and Scottish rules on evidence differ from those in England and Wales. We plan research, interviews and document handling with Scottish solicitors from the outset, so material is gathered lawfully and in a form usable in Scottish proceedings.
